description: Experience the true taste of the South with our classic Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken recipe. Each piece is marinated to perfection, creating a tender, juicy interior and an irresistibly crispy, golden-brown crust. This iconic dish is pure comfort food, perfect for any gathering or a satisfying family meal.

ingredients.item: Bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (drumsticks, thighs, breasts)

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl or resealable bag, combine the chicken pieces, buttermilk, and hot sauce (if using). Ensure all chicken is submerged. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the buttermilk to tenderize the chicken and infuse flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dredging Mixture
instructions.text: In a separate shallow dish or large resealable bag, whisk together the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, salt, black pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne pepper until well combined. This is your seasoned flour mixture.

instructions.title: Dredge the Chicken
instructions.text: Remove the chicken from the buttermilk marinade, allowing any excess to drip off. Do not rinse. Place each piece of chicken into the seasoned flour mixture, ensuring it is thoroughly coated. Press the flour onto the chicken to create a thick crust. Shake off any excess flour and place the dredged chicken on a wire rack set over a baking sheet. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes to allow the coating to adhere.

instructions.title: Heat the Frying Oil
instructions.text: Pour the vegetable or peanut oil into a large, heavy-bottomed pot, Dutch oven, or deep fryer. The oil should be at least 3-4 inches deep. Heat the oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 325-350°F (160-175°C). Use a candy thermometer or deep-fry thermometer to monitor the temperature accurately.

instructions.title: Fry the Chicken in Batches
instructions.text: Carefully lower 3-4 pieces of chicken into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Overcrowding will lower the oil temperature and result in greasy chicken. Fry for about 6-8 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until the chicken is golden brown and cooked through. The internal temperature should reach 165°F (74°C). Dark meat pieces like thighs and drumsticks may take slightly longer than breasts.

instructions.title: Drain and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, carefully remove the fried chicken from the oil using tongs and place it on a clean wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain any excess oil. Lightly sprinkle with a pinch of extra salt immediately after removing from the oil. Repeat with remaining chicken batches, ensuring the oil returns to the correct temperature between batches. Serve hot and enjoy!

tips: For extra crispy chicken, double dip! After the first dredge in flour, dip the chicken back into the remaining buttermilk (or a mixture of buttermilk and a little water) and then dredge again in the seasoned flour.
Do not overcrowd the pot when frying. Frying in smaller batches is crucial for maintaining oil temperature and achieving that perfect crispy crust.
Always let your fried chicken rest on a wire rack, not paper towels. This allows air to circulate, keeping the crust crispy instead of steaming and becoming soggy.
